data.title: apps/invoicing: client email format validation belongs in the clients repository

data.to:
Found while planning AS-65 (cto-owen, 2026-09-02). Non-blocking for AS-46/AS-47.

THE GAP. repos.clients.create validates name and email with assertText alone — non-empty string, trimmed. "not an email" is accepted and stored. The DDL CHECK is the same predicate (length(trim(email)) > 0), so there is no format enforcement anywhere between a form field and the row.

WHY IT MATTERS. lib/invoices/lifecycle.js ensureCustomer hands client.email to Stripe at invoice FINALIZE. A malformed address is refused there — late, on the wrong screen, as a 502, long after the freelancer typed it. And docs/design/wireframes/00-flows.md Flow 3 step 3a names "malformed email" as a validation state the screens are expected to render (S{4,6}-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION), so the ledger already assumes enforcement that does not exist.

WHERE IT BELONGS, and this is the whole point of filing it separately. The REPOSITORY, beside the row, where the constraint cannot be bypassed. AS-65 deliberately did NOT add a shape check at routes/clients.js: a check at the route is a second source of truth that the still-callable repository walks straight past — the exact drift routes/contracts.js's banner and the AS-42 plan argue against.

PRIOR ART TO READ, NOT TO IMPORT WHOLESALE. lib/auth/accounts.js has assertEmailShape (length <= 254, exactly one @, not first or last character, no whitespace). It is private to that module, throws AuthError, and is about the FREELANCER's own sign-in address — deliverability to the account holder, not to a client. Decide in planning whether to lift it to lib/db/errors.js as an assertEmail alongside assertText/assertStripeId (one validator, two callers) or to keep two. If it is lifted, accounts.js must keep answering AuthError to its own callers, or test/auth.test.js's sign-up cases move.

SCOPE NOTE. Also consider the length-ceiling question AS-65 section 9 Q5 parked: there is no max length on client name or email today. Same layer, same task if the planner agrees.

ACCEPTANCE: the check lives in exactly one place and the route adds none; a malformed client email is a ValidationError naming the field, and no row is written; existing clients.create call sites in test/repositories.test.js, test/contracts.test.js and test/invoices.test.js still pass or are updated deliberately; a falsification recipe shows the new guard red once per the house technique; no migration unless the planner argues for a CHECK (the existing rows are all test rows, but state the position); no new dependencies — a regex or a hand-rolled predicate, never an email-validation package.

Oldest ready medium by age under the 2026-09-11 scheduling rule (AS-103 still gated: no hooks block in .claude/settings.json; AS-50 waits on AS-51). Complexity low, so the two-stage path applies (CLAUDE.md § Employee Execution Model, 'Scaled by complexity'): developer-marcus writes the plan, commits it to master, creates feat/AS-67-client-email-validation and .worktrees/AS-67, and implements in the same stage; a qa-* reviews next tick. Proof burden for low: suite green with a --build receipt plus one observed red per falsifier the plan names. If Marcus finds it is not low, he says so here, re-marks it, and hands it back to the three-stage path before writing code.

Plan + implement stage (two-stage path, complexity low — confirmed low after exploration). Marcus on Opus under the Fable fallback (Fable spawn refused, HTTP 429). Tick watcher:79108 loop tick 14.

PLAN: .lattice/plans/task_01M1J4ZQYVS7X8Z5HEPSH2YKWD.md (9eae160). Decisions: D1 one predicate, two vocabularies — isEmailShape/assertEmail/EMAIL_MAX in lib/db/errors.js, lifted verbatim from accounts.js's private copy; accounts.js keeps assertEmailShape → AuthError('invalid-email') as a one-line wrapper; auth.test.js untouched. D2 predicate exactly as before (one @, not first/last, no whitespace, ≤254), no trimming in the repository. D3 email ceiling 254 yes (inherent), name ceiling declined — no consumer has named a number; box stated. D4 no migration — DDL CHECK stays non-empty; a shape CHECK is a clients table rebuild under two composite-FK referrers for a rule the repository already makes unbypassable. D5 findByEmail keeps assertText (a read should not refuse). D6 routes/clients.js untouched.

BRANCH: feat/AS-67-client-email-validation, tip c5e1fdb (1 commit, 6 files +100/-9): lib/db/errors.js, lib/db/database.js (re-export isEmailShape), lib/db/repositories/clients.js (create + update use assertEmail), lib/auth/accounts.js, test/repositories.test.js (+C9 create refuses 7 shapes/no row/254 accepted, +C10 update refuses/row byte-identical), test/clients.test.js (L4 +3 malformed rows, cardinality 10). AC3 grep: indexOf('@') hits lib/db/errors.js once, nothing else. AC5/AC7: routes/, package*.json, migrations/ have an empty diff against master.

RECEIPTS (compose-run.mjs, docker by absolute path; all torn down, leak check clean each run):
- green asc-impl-as67-green: 'Image asc-impl-as67-green-test Built', 494/475/0/19 — matches the plan's predicted 494 (baseline 492 + C9 + C10).
- final asc-impl-as67-final (rebuilt after the last mutant restore): 'Image asc-impl-as67-final-test Built', 494/475/0/19.

FALSIFIERS (in place, applied-at-site asserted by scratchpad/agent-developer-marcus/AS-67/mutate.mjs, restored with git checkout, git diff --exit-code clean after each; the sandbox refused 'trap', so the restore is explicit and verified rather than trapped):
- F1 create → assertText: 'Image asc-impl-as67-f1-test Built', 494/473/2 — red {C9, L4}. Exact.
- F2 update → assertText: 'Image asc-impl-as67-f2-test Built', 494/474/1 — red {C10}. Exact.
- F3 isEmailShape → any string: 'Image asc-impl-as67-f3-test Built', 494/468/7 — red {C9, C10, L4, H6} + 3 screens.test.js S1 cases ('S1-ERROR-VALIDATION re-renders every non-sensitive submitted value…', 'a value containing markup is rendered as text…', 'the submitted password is never re-rendered…'), which drive sign-up with 'not-an-email'. - F4 EMAIL_MAX → 1000: 'Image asc-impl-as67-f4-test Built', 494/472/3 — red {C9, C10, H6}. WIDER than the plan's {C9, H6} by C10, which shares the MALFORMED_EMAILS table (255-char entry). Classified benign; the plan under-predicted.

FOR THE REVIEWER (Ruben or Priya): plan §4 AC1–AC8, §6 for what to run; §7 names the residual in the open — the invoice form's intent=add-client now answers text/plain 400 on a malformed or trailing-space email (screen wrapper's generic refusal) instead of storing it; not the S4-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION re-render, which is the screen's surface (view model only knows 'required'). That is a behaviour gap for Owen to triage under the comments-first rule, not a route-level check. Probe ideas: unicode whitespace (\s matches U+00A0 and U+2003 — refused), '@' alone, 'a@b' (accepted by design, as C1 always did). Not transitioned to review — Owen does, --no-auto-review.

Stage closed by the orchestrator (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 14): in_progress -> review (--no-auto-review). Marcus ran on Opus under the Fable fallback (Fable refused at HTTP 429). Kept low; tip c5e1fdb on feat/AS-67-client-email-validation. Assigned qa-ruben for next tick's review (Priya as fallback if he is busy). Triage note on Marcus's §7 residual (invoice-form intent=add-client now answers a text/plain 400 on a malformed email instead of an S4-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION re-render): it is a behaviour gap on AS-46's surface — the reviewer should look at it and say whether it is a defect to file or a coverage residual to fold into the next task touching lib/screens/invoice-form-view.js.

Review stage opens (cto-owen, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 15): Ruben reviews cold in .worktrees/AS-67 against git diff master...feat/AS-67-client-email-validation. The open residual named at the review transition (invoice-form add-client text/plain 400 vs the S4 validation re-render) is his to classify.

VERDICT: PASS. No inline fix, nothing committed on the branch; tip stays c5e1fdb. Ruben (agent:qa-ruben) on Opus under the Fable fallback, tick watcher:79108 loop tick 15. Reviewed cold in .worktrees/AS-67 from the plan and `git diff master...feat/AS-67-client-email-validation` (6 files, +100/-9); I read Marcus's stage comment LAST, after every number below was already in my scratchpad — his F1-F4 sets and mine agree independently. No daemon/generic-actor comment exists on this record.

FINDINGS (4; none blocks). Findings outside the AC list: 4. Tags: defect = argued from criteria and blocks; convention/residual = recorded, routed, never a verdict.

1. [behaviour defect — NOT this task's; for Owen's triage gate] Invoice-form `intent=add-client` with an ordinary typo answers a bare text/plain 400 and drops the half-filled invoice form. Observed, not argued (route probe in a scratch copy of the image, compose-probe.log): `POST /invoices/new intent=add-client clientEmail='not-an-email'` -> 400 text/plain `ValidationError: screen-create`, 0 rows; same for `'ann@example.test '` (trailing space) and `' ann@example.test'` (leading space); `'x'*246+'@ex.test'` (254) -> 200 S4-DEFAULT-CREATE, row written; 255 -> 400. Cause: `routes/invoices.js` case 'add-client' calls `repos.clients.create` outside any try, so the repository's ValidationError falls to the `screen()` wrapper's generic `fail()`; `lib/screens/invoice-form-view.js clientFieldErrors` knows only "required", so S4-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION (wireframes Flow 3 step 3a, "malformed email") is specified and never rendered. Pre-AS-67 the same input was stored and refused by Stripe at finalize as a 502 on the wrong screen — AS-67 is strictly better (earlier, no bad row) and the plan scoped this out in D6/§7 with the task description's own "non-blocking for AS-46/AS-47", so it does not block. Classification for the record: a behaviour defect in shipped code (customer-visible wrong output reachable by a copy-pasted trailing space), on AS-46's screen surface, priority medium under the 2026-09-11 rule — and its scope is WIDER than §7 says: AS-127 merged after this branch's base and `routes/contracts.js:208` on master has the identical add-client shape, so screen 6 (S6-CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION) has the same gap. One task, not two: trim `clientEmail` at both screens before `findByEmail`/`create`, and catch the repository's ValidationError in the add-client case the way the save case already catches it (`clientRefused`), rendering the CLIENT-ERROR-VALIDATION state. Not a route-level check (D6 stands): the screen rendering a refusal the repository already made is not a second source of truth.

2. [convention — plan record accuracy, no code change] Two of the four predicted red sets in plan §4 are narrower than the observed sets. F3 predicted {C9, C10, L4, H6}, observed 7: those four plus three `test/screens.test.js` cases ('S1-ERROR-VALIDATION re-renders every non-sensitive submitted value…', 'a value containing markup is rendered as text…', 'the submitted password is never re-rendered…') — screens.test.js:298 drives `not-an-email` through sign-up. F4 predicted {C9, H6}, observed {C9, C10, H6} — C10 iterates the same MALFORMED_EMAILS table whose 7th entry is the 255-char case. Both are the plan under-counting the predicate's dependents, not the guard under-covering; wider is the good direction, and F3's extra three are the strongest proof AC3 has (screen 1 rides the lifted copy too). Routed to the plan's owner as a record note; nothing to change on the branch.

3. [residual for the record — fold into the next task touching lib/db/errors.js, do not file] The 254 ceiling counts UTF-16 code units, not the RFC 5321 octets it cites. Probe: 126 U+1F600 + '@x' = 254 `.length`, 128 code points, 508 bytes -> accepted; 127 + '@x' = 256 units -> refused. Lifted verbatim, so sign-up has always behaved this way; no consumer names an octet limit today. Same bucket, deliberately-weak-by-design and noted only: U+200B/U+200D and NUL pass (not `\s`), `a@.` passes, `Ann<ann@x.test>` passes; U+00A0 and U+3000 are refused (`\s`). 35 host-side probe inputs, 0 surprises against D2 as written.

4. [convention — plan §6 recipe] The host-side red recipe (`node --test test/repositories.test.js …`) is not runnable from a worktree: no node_modules, and `npm ci` is off the tick allowlist. Every red here went through compose `--build` instead, which is the higher-fidelity path anyway. Note for future low-complexity plans: name the compose route as the recipe and host-side as the optional shortcut.

MERGE SEAM: master moved 9eae160 -> 15dc3ba under this branch (AS-56, AS-127). File overlap between master's post-base changes and the branch: none. `test/auth.test.js` changed on master (G15 route count 27 -> 29 for screen 6) and is untouched on the branch, so master's copy wins cleanly; H6 is identical on both sides. Predicted merged-master count: 511 + 2 = 513 / 494 pass / 0 / 19.

- AC2 update refuses the same and leaves the row byte-identical: C10 green (deepEqual pre-row, name untouched); F2 red. Pass.

Probe past the list (M6): 35 predicate inputs host-side (unicode whitespace, zero-width, NUL, astral-length boundary, non-string types, String object), 3 route surfaces in the image (invoice form add-client, POST /clients, sign-up — the sign-up leg hit the origin guard because my probe omitted the header; H6 + F3 already cover it), commit identity (developer-marcus, actor-id form), README stale-prose grep (none). Budget spent: yes; the review did not stop at the list.
